text:
Predicates:
ContainsKnowledge(x) ::: x contains knowledge.
Reads(x, y) ::: x reads y.
GainsKnowledge(x) ::: x gains knowledge.
Smarter(x) ::: x becomes smarter.
Book(y) ::: y is a book.
Author(y, z) ::: y is the author of z.
Title(y, t) ::: y has the title t.
Premises:
Books contain tons of knowledge ::: ∀x (Book(x) → ContainsKnowledge(x))
When a person reads a book, that person gains knowledge ::: ∀x ∀y (Reads(x, y) ∧ Book(y) → GainsKnowledge(x))
If a person gains knowledge, they become smarter ::: ∀x (GainsKnowledge(x) → Smarter(x))
Harry read the book “Walden” by Henry Thoreau ::: Reads(harry, walden) ∧ Author(walden, henryThoreau) ∧ Title(walden, “Walden”)
Conclusion:
Walden contains knowledge ::: ContainsKnowledge(walden)
